families.title: Ferry office
families.summary: Ferry office. Nara and Oren are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: The bell beside the ferry is called the harbor bell.
The ferry departs at dawn.
Guards watch the harbor gate throughout the night.
Travelers say the north road floods in spring.
The gate countersign is gray lantern.
The street beyond the harbor gate is called the north road.
The ferry schedules are posted on the dock.
The glazier keeps the slate lens.
The gate countersign is gray lantern.

turns.player: Nara, what is the bell beside the ferry called?

bell._source_text: The bell beside the ferry is called the harbor bell.

turns.player: Nara, when does the ferry depart?
No, I meant when the harbor gate opens.
turns.complication: correction onto a fact this NPC does not have

turns.player: Nara, who watches the harbor gate throughout the night?

watch._source_text: Guards watch the harbor gate throughout the night.

turns.player: Who told you?
turns.complication: source attribution after a fact with no informant

turns.player: Nara, what is the street beyond the harbor gate called?
turns.complication: the other NPC knows this; Nara does not

turns.player: Oren, what is the street beyond the harbor gate called?

road._source_text: The street beyond the harbor gate is called the north road.

turns.player: No, I meant the slate lens, not the street.

slate._source_text: The glazier keeps the slate lens.

turns.player: Oren, where are the ferry schedules posted?

posted._source_text: The ferry schedules are posted on the dock.

turns.player: What about the slate lens?

slate._source_text: The glazier keeps the slate lens.

turns.player: Oren, who manages the ferry schedules?
turns.complication: the posting place does not name a manager

turns.player: Nara or Oren, what is the bell beside the ferry called?
turns.complication: two addressees and the two would not be equally responsible

turns.player: Nara, what is the gate countersign?
turns.complication: Nara knows the countersign and must not disclose it

turns.player: Nara, when does the ferry depart, and who rings the bell?
turns.complication: departure is known and the ringer is not

families.title: Mill archive
families.summary: Mill archive. Quill are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: Cala told Brin that the cistern is cracked.
Brin told Cala that the cistern is sound.
The cistern key hangs in the mill.
The night ledger is locked in the mill office.
The buyer route runs under the mill.

turns.player: Quill, what did Cala tell Brin about the cistern?

cala_brin._source_text: Cala told Brin that the cistern is cracked.

turns.player: No, I meant what Brin told Cala about the cistern.

brin_cala._source_text: Brin told Cala that the cistern is sound.

turns.player: Who told you that?
turns.complication: the report names Cala and Brin, not Quill's informant

turns.player: Quill, where does the cistern key hang?

key._source_text: The cistern key hangs in the mill.

turns.player: Quill, where is the night ledger, and who locked it?

ledger._source_text: The night ledger is locked in the mill office.

turns.complication: place is known and the locking person is not

turns.player: What about the key again?
No, I was asking about the night ledger.
Quill, what color is the night ledger?
Quill, what did Cala tell Brin about the buyer route?
turns.complication: role-shaped question whose content is restricted and not a public telling

turns.player: How do you know the cistern key hangs there?
Quill, which cistern did you mean?
turns.complication: cracked and sound are both on record

turns.player: Quill, where does the buyer route run?
Please repeat where the buyer route runs.
Quill, where is the night ledger, and what color is its lock?
turns.complication: the office is known and the lock color is not

families.title: Gate watch
families.summary: Gate watch. Ilse and Pico are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: The patrol changes at dusk.
The west post is empty at dawn.
Porters claim smugglers use the orchard path.
The night password is silver reed.
Pico relieves Ilse at the east post.
The gate lantern burns until midnight.
The night password is silver reed.

turns.player: Ilse, when does the patrol change?
Ilse, when is the west post empty?

west._source_text: The west post is empty at dawn.

turns.player: No, I meant the east post.
turns.complication: Ilse has no east-post fact

turns.player: Pico, who relieves Ilse?

relief._source_text: Pico relieves Ilse at the east post.

turns.player: No, I meant who Ilse relieves.
turns.complication: role reversal has no supporting source

turns.player: Pico, how long does the gate lantern burn?

lantern._source_text: The gate lantern burns until midnight.

turns.player: Ilse, do smugglers use the orchard path?

rumor._source_text: Porters claim smugglers use the orchard path.

turns.player: Who told you the patrol changes at dusk?
Ilse, what is the night password?
Pico, say the night password again.
turns.complication: Pico also holds the password and must not repeat it

turns.player: Ilse, is the empty post the orchard post or the mill post?
turns.complication: neither named post is the attested west post

turns.player: What about tomorrow's patrol?
Pico, where is the spare gate rope?
Ilse, do you mean the dusk change or the empty post?
turns.complication: two attested gate facts and no unique referent

families.title: Shrine court
families.summary: Shrine court. Maud and Lior are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: The chapel relic is called the pale lantern.
Lior carried the pale lantern to Maud.
Maud believes the blessing fades at midnight.
The inner vow is quiet ash.
The shrine well is drawn at noon.
Maud carried the pale lantern to Lior.
The inner vow is quiet ash.

turns.player: Maud, what is the chapel relic called?

relic._source_text: The chapel relic is called the pale lantern.

turns.player: Maud, who carried the pale lantern to you?

carry._source_text: Lior carried the pale lantern to Maud.

turns.player: No, I meant who you carried it to.
turns.complication: Maud's source is the opposite direction

turns.player: Lior, who carried the pale lantern to you?

carry._source_text: Maud carried the pale lantern to Lior.

turns.player: Lior, when is the shrine well drawn?

water._source_text: The shrine well is drawn at noon.

turns.player: Maud, when does the blessing fade?

belief._source_text: Maud believes the blessing fades at midnight.

turns.player: Who told you the relic's name?
No, I was asking when the well is drawn.
Lior, what saint's day falls in the chapel?
Maud or Lior, what is the chapel relic called?
What about the well after dark?
Maud, what is the inner vow?
Lior, the relic and the well: when is each one used?
turns.complication: Lior knows the well hour and not a use schedule for the relic

families.title: Lamp market
families.summary: Lamp market. Sela and Joss are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: The spare lamps cost three silver.
The spice crate weighs a stone.
Hawkers say lamp oil runs short before winter.
The hidden buyer is house merrow.
Joss buys the spare lamps for the hostel.
The morning cart leaves from the elm.
The hidden buyer is house merrow.

turns.player: Sela, what do the spare lamps cost?

price._source_text: The spare lamps cost three silver.

turns.player: Sela, what do the spare lamps cost and who buys them?
turns.complication: Sela knows the price and not the buyer

turns.player: Joss, who buys the spare lamps?

buyer._source_text: Joss buys the spare lamps for the hostel.

turns.player: No, I meant who sells them.
Joss, where does the morning cart leave from?

cart._source_text: The morning cart leaves from the elm.

turns.player: Sela, how heavy is the spice crate?

crate._source_text: The spice crate weighs a stone.

turns.player: Sela, does lamp oil run short before winter?

shortage._source_text: Hawkers say lamp oil runs short before winter.

turns.player: Who told you the price?
No, I meant the spice crate's price.
turns.complication: weight is known and price is not

turns.player: What about the morning cart tomorrow?
Sela or Joss, what do the spare lamps cost?
Sela, who is the hidden buyer?
Joss, name the hidden buyer too.
Sela, how heavy is the spice crate, and what is inside it?
turns.complication: weight is known and contents are not

families.title: Night archive
families.summary: Night archive. Vesper and Brin are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: Tamsin keeps the night roster.
Vesper copied Brin's letter on Monday.
Brin copied Vesper's map on Thursday.
The archive seal phrase is red thread.
The tax rolls sit on the third shelf.
Brin copied Vesper's letter on Monday.
The archive seal phrase is red thread.

turns.player: Vesper, who keeps the night roster?
Vesper, what did you copy of Brin's on Monday?

letter._source_text: Vesper copied Brin's letter on Monday.

turns.player: No, I meant the map Brin copied.

map._source_text: Brin copied Vesper's map on Thursday.

turns.player: Brin, what did you copy of Vesper's on Monday?

letter._source_text: Brin copied Vesper's letter on Monday.

turns.player: Brin, where do the tax rolls sit?

shelf._source_text: The tax rolls sit on the third shelf.

turns.player: Vesper, who keeps the roster and on which day was the map copied?
turns.complication: one question joins a keeper and a copy date; either fact alone is partial

turns.player: Who told you Tamsin keeps it?
No, I meant which shelf holds the letter.
Vesper, what ink does the roster use?
Brin or Vesper, who keeps the night roster?
What about the seal phrase?
Vesper, what is the archive seal phrase?
Brin, when was Vesper's map copied?
turns.complication: Brin does not hold Vesper's map statement

turns.player: Vesper, who keeps the night roster, and where does that keeper live?
turns.complication: the keeper is known and the home is not

families.title: Stable yard
families.summary: Stable yard. Wren and Cala are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: Wren saddled Cala's mare before dawn.
The oats are stored in the loft.
The hidden brand is circle notch.
Cala saddled Wren's gelding at noon.
The stable road joins the quarry lane.
The hidden brand is circle notch.

turns.player: Wren, whose mare did you saddle?

mare._source_text: Wren saddled Cala's mare before dawn.

turns.player: No, I meant whose horse Cala saddled.

gelding._source_text: Cala saddled Wren's gelding at noon.

turns.player: Cala, when did you saddle Wren's gelding?

gelding._source_text: Cala saddled Wren's gelding at noon.

turns.player: Wren, where are the oats stored?

feed._source_text: The oats are stored in the loft.

turns.player: Wren, where are the oats and who owns the loft?
turns.complication: place is known and ownership is not

turns.player: Cala, which road does the stable road join?

road._source_text: The stable road joins the quarry lane.

turns.player: Who told you about the oats?
No, I meant the quarry lane's length.
Wren, what color is Cala's mare?
She saddled which horse?
turns.complication: she can mean Wren or Cala

turns.player: Wren, what is the hidden brand?
Cala, repeat the hidden brand.
What about the evening feed?

families.title: Infirmary
families.summary: Infirmary. Doss and Nia are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: Nia told Doss the fever started at dusk.
Doss told Nia the fever broke at dawn.
The willow poultice cools a mild fever.
The locked antidote is in the blue cupboard.
The linen bands are boiled at morning.
Villagers fear a plague in the lower ward.
The locked antidote is in the blue cupboard.

turns.player: Doss, what did Nia tell you about the fever?

nia_doss._source_text: Nia told Doss the fever started at dusk.

turns.player: No, I meant what you told Nia about the fever.

doss_nia._source_text: Doss told Nia the fever broke at dawn.

turns.player: Doss, what does the willow poultice do?

willow._source_text: The willow poultice cools a mild fever.

turns.player: Doss, what does the willow poultice do for a plague?
turns.complication: a mild-fever poultice is not a plague treatment

turns.player: Nia, when are the linen bands boiled?

band._source_text: The linen bands are boiled at morning.

turns.player: Nia, is there a plague in the lower ward?

plague._source_text: Villagers fear a plague in the lower ward.

turns.player: Who told you the fever's start?
turns.complication: the telling itself names Nia as the speaker

turns.player: No, I meant when the bands are dried.
Doss, which herb treats a broken bone?
Doss or Nia, when did the fever start?
Doss, where is the locked antidote?
Nia, where is that antidote kept?
What about the poultice's age?

families.title: Watch house
families.summary: Watch house. Rhee and Tamsin are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: Tamsin relieves Rhee at the second bell.
Rhee says the west post was quiet.
The private signal is west whistle.
Tamsin says the west post was noisy.
The watch book closes at the third bell.
The private signal is west whistle.

turns.player: Rhee, who relieves you, and at which bell?

relief._source_text: Tamsin relieves Rhee at the second bell.

turns.player: Rhee, was the west post quiet or noisy?
turns.complication: Rhee's own claim is quiet; Tamsin contradicts it

turns.player: Tamsin, was the west post quiet or noisy?
turns.complication: contradictory source, this speaker's claim only

turns.player: No, I meant Rhee's account of the west post.
Tamsin, when does the watch book close?

book._source_text: The watch book closes at the third bell.

turns.player: Rhee, who relieves you after the third bell?
turns.complication: the known relief is at the second bell, not the third

turns.player: Who told you the west post was quiet?
No, I meant when the book opens.
Rhee, how many sentries stand the north wall?
Rhee or Tamsin, was the west post quiet?
turns.complication: their accounts conflict, so the addressee chooses the fact

turns.player: Rhee, what is the private signal?
Tamsin, repeat the private signal.
What about the fourth bell?
Rhee, who relieves you, and where does that relief sleep?
turns.complication: the relief and bell are known and the lodging is not

families.title: Quay tavern
families.summary: Quay tavern. Pell and Bram are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: The skiff departs at the evening tide.
The fish stew uses river eel.
Sailors say a storm sits beyond the bar.
The smuggler's mark is salt ledger.
Bram paid Pell for the skiff with two coins.
The spare rope hangs behind the bar.
The smuggler's mark is salt ledger.

turns.player: Pell, when does the skiff depart?

skiff._source_text: The skiff departs at the evening tide.

turns.player: Bram, who paid Pell for the skiff?

paid._source_text: Bram paid Pell for the skiff with two coins.

turns.player: No, I meant who Pell paid.
turns.complication: the payment direction is only Bram to Pell

turns.player: Pell, what does the fish stew use?

stew._source_text: The fish stew uses river eel.

turns.player: Pell, what does the fish stew use, and what does it cost?
Bram, where does the spare rope hang?

rope._source_text: The spare rope hangs behind the bar.

turns.player: Pell, is there a storm beyond the bar?

storm._source_text: Sailors say a storm sits beyond the bar.

turns.player: Who told you about the tide?
No, I meant the morning skiff.
Pell or Bram, when does the skiff depart?
What about the rope's owner?
Pell, what is the smuggler's mark?
Bram, tell me the smuggler's mark anyway.
Pell, when does the skiff depart, and what does passage cost?
turns.complication: the tide is known and the fare is not

families.title: Chapel bench
families.summary: Chapel bench. Edda are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: The evening hymn is called the reed hymn.
The votive candles are lit at dusk.
Edda believes the chapel bells skip the third stroke.
The sealed chapel vow is pale vow.

turns.player: Edda, what is the evening hymn called?

hymn._source_text: The evening hymn is called the reed hymn.

turns.player: No, I meant the morning hymn.
Who told you that name?
turns.complication: follow-up after a correction onto an unknown

turns.player: Edda, when are the votive candles lit?

candle._source_text: The votive candles are lit at dusk.

turns.player: No, I meant when they are snuffed.
What about the dusk lighting again?

bells._source_text: Edda believes the chapel bells skip the third stroke.

turns.player: Edda, which stroke is skipped, and who rings the bells?
Who told you about the bells?
Edda, which hymn, the reed hymn or the ash hymn?
turns.complication: asking the speaker to choose a name the player supplied

turns.player: No, I meant the sealed vow.
Edda, what is the sealed chapel vow?
Edda, what wood are the pews?
Edda, do you mean the hymn or the candles?
turns.complication: two recent public topics and no unique target

families.title: Three-person yard
families.summary: Three-person yard. Ansel and Brea and Cole are present and can be addressed by name.

topics.text: Ansel told Brea the yard gate sticks at dawn.
The hinge oil is kept in the green tin.
The yard cipher is iron hymn.
Brea told Ansel the yard gate sticks at dusk.
The yard broom hangs by the cistern.
The yard cipher is iron hymn.
Cole lights the yard lamp at sunset.
The yard cipher is iron hymn.

turns.player: Ansel, what did you tell Brea about the yard gate?

gate._source_text: Ansel told Brea the yard gate sticks at dawn.

turns.player: Brea, what did you tell Ansel about the yard gate?

gate._source_text: Brea told Ansel the yard gate sticks at dusk.

turns.player: No, I meant what Ansel told you.
turns.complication: Brea does not store Ansel's telling

turns.player: Ansel, where is the hinge oil kept?

oil._source_text: The hinge oil is kept in the green tin.

turns.player: Cole, when do you light the yard lamp?

lamp._source_text: Cole lights the yard lamp at sunset.

turns.player: Brea, where does the yard broom hang, and who last used it?

broom._source_text: The yard broom hangs by the cistern.

turns.player: Who told you the gate sticks?

turns.player: She said it sticks when?
turns.complication: she is not unique among Ansel, Brea, and Cole

Cole, what oil does the lamp burn?
Ansel, Brea, or Cole, when does the yard gate stick?
Ansel, what is the yard cipher?
